defects.before: - `--seq` selects the interval mode. The comment says that its code is the text of bwx.c. The whole-chip test uses this mode only.
defects.after: - `--seq ...` names the interval mode. The comment says that its code is the text of bwx.c. `main` runs this mode when no argument is the word `--trial` (lines 2912 to 2914). The whole-chip test uses this mode only.
defects.evidence: Lines 2912 to 2914 of bwx12.c choose the mode only by the word `--trial`; `--seq` (line 2948) only fills the kernel list, so it does not select a mode.

defects.before: The build record gives 24 for both versions [Ref2].
defects.after: The build record (the file build.txt that the build script wrote on CRB) gives the start address 24 modulo 64 for both versions [Ref2].
defects.evidence: The number 24 had no meaning clause and "build record" was not defined at first use; crb-build-1/build.txt lines 9 and 14 say `placement ... (start modulo 64): call=24` for bwx12 and bwx11, and build12.sh writes build.txt.

defects.before: The listing confirms it: the sums are in the registers v24 to v31 [Ref1].
defects.after: The machine-code listing of the CRB binary confirms it: the sums are in the registers v24 to v31 [Ref1].
defects.evidence: This is the first use of "the listing" in the companion and the overview word list has no entry for it; crb-build-1/listing.txt shows the adds into v24 to v31 at 0x4680 to 0x469c.

defects.before: A failed `mprotect` only prints a message, and the run continues. In the test every stderr.txt is empty [Ref5].
defects.after: A failed `mprotect` only prints a message, and the run continues. The script rx.sh writes the error output of the program to the file stderr.txt [Ref3]. In the test every stderr.txt is empty [Ref5].
defects.evidence: The file name stderr.txt was used without a definition; rx.sh line 17 appends the error output of the program to it (`2>> $out/stderr.txt`), and `wc -c` gives 0 bytes for all 9 result folders.

defects.before: - Machine code, once per call [Ref1]: the 8 sum registers are stored to the stack and loaded back, 7 vector adds and one `addp` (it adds the two 64-bit halves of one register) add them into one number, and `fmov x0, d31` copies the result into the return register x0.
defects.after: - Machine code, once per call [Ref1]: the 8 sum registers are stored to the stack and loaded back. Then 7 vector adds and one `addp` add them into one number. `addp` adds the two 64-bit halves of one register. `fmov x0, d31` copies the result into the return register x0.
defects.evidence: One sentence carried three claims plus a parenthesis (plain-English rules 2 and 3); the content matches listing.txt 0x46a8 to 0x4708 (4 stp, 4 ldp, 7 vector adds, 1 addp, fmov).

defects.before: One paragraph of 5 sentences: "Builds a CPU set that holds only `cpu` ... before it maps its buffer."
defects.after:
The same sentences as 4 bullets: "- Builds a CPU set that holds only `cpu` and passes it to `sched_setaffinity`. The first argument 0 means the calling thread.
- After the call Linux runs this thread on that CPU only.
- A failure ends the program with exit status 2.
- Each worker calls the function at its start (line 1642), before it opens its counters and before it maps its buffer."
defects.evidence: Section 5 of the brief limits a text to 1 to 4 short sentences or up to 6 bullets; the paragraph had 5 sentences.

defects.before: One paragraph of 5 sentences: "`p` is the read position. ... After it x1 holds `end`."
defects.after: The same sentences as 3 bullets: "- `p` is the read position. `end` is the first address after the range: `a` plus `n` words.\n- Machine code, once per call and before the loop: `add x1, x0, x1, lsl #3` [Ref1].\n- Before this instruction the register x0 holds `a` and x1 holds `n`. After it x1 holds `end`."
defects.evidence: Section 5 of the brief limits a text to 1 to 4 short sentences or up to 6 bullets; the paragraph had 5 sentences.

defects.after: heading added: "Function `k_oldread2`: A/A copy, not run in the test"
defects.evidence: Section 5 asks for a heading on the first segment of every top-level function; line 475 creates the function `k_oldread2`, and the rows of `k_oldread`, `k_oldwrite` and `k_oldcopy` already have one.

defects.before: Pad values without a unit in four rows (189-206, 216-224, 228-236, 237-252), for example "32 for `copy`, ... and 48 for `asmcopy_c`", "`asmwrite` (32)", "which is 0".
defects.after: The unit B added to each pad value, for example "32 B for `copy`, `asmcopy`, `asmcopy2` and `asmcopy_c_reg`, and 48 B for `asmcopy_c` and `asmcopy_c_add`", "`asmwrite` (32 B)", "which is 0 B".
defects.evidence: A pad is a number of bytes (`.fill N, 1, 0` in line 163), the row of lines 174 to 188 already writes "4 B or 20 B", and the values 32 and 48 were confirmed with `gcc -E` plus a small C test of `PADOF`.

defects.after:
- `stop_common` = 1 (`--stop common`).
- `start_offset` = 0 (`--start common`): every thread starts each interval at byte 0 of its own buffer (line 1662). This option chooses a place in the buffer. It does not set the start time of an interval.
defects.evidence: Line 1662 of bwx12.c sets `off` to 0 when `cfg.start_offset` is 0 and line 1693 starts the timed loop at `at = off`, while the word list of the overview defines "common start" as the start time `t_sched_ns`, so the row gave the reader no meaning for `--start common` and invited the wrong one.
